about: Timeline sort pool, hand-kept (docs/features/timeline-sort/design.md §4.2). when = widest window of years over every dating system the site recognises; historians' years, negative = BC, no year 0; null = an open edge. shown:false = early Genesis, order only. anchor = how the window was set, recomputed by the build. Never delete an event after launch: mark it "retired": true. resolutions = one-line notes for the build's cross-check warnings. After editing run: node --experimental-strip-types scripts/build-timeline.ts

events.label: God creates the heavens and the earth
events.dating: In the beginning, before anything else in the Bible's story (Genesis 1). Early Genesis gives no dates historians can use, so no year is shown.

events.label: God forms Adam from the dust of the ground
events.dating: On the sixth day of creation (Genesis 1:31; 2:7). Early Genesis gives no dates historians can use, so no year is shown.

events.label: God makes Eve from Adam's rib
events.dating: In the Garden of Eden, after Adam was made (Genesis 2). Early Genesis gives no dates historians can use, so no year is shown.

events.label: Adam and Eve are sent out of Eden
events.dating: After the first sin, before Adam and Eve had children (Genesis 3–4). Early Genesis gives no dates historians can use, so no year is shown.

events.label: Cain kills his brother Abel
events.dating: In the first family, before Seth was born to replace Abel (Genesis 4). Early Genesis gives no dates historians can use, so no year is shown.

events.label: Seth is born to Adam and Eve
events.dating: When Adam was 130, after Abel's death (Genesis 4:25; 5:3). Early Genesis gives no dates historians can use, so no year is shown.

events.label: Enoch walks with God and is taken away
events.dating: Before the Flood, in Adam's line, seven generations from Adam (Genesis 5; Jude 14). Early Genesis gives no dates historians can use, so no year is shown.

events.label: Lamech's son Noah is born
events.dating: Before the Flood, ten generations from Adam (Genesis 5). Early Genesis gives no dates historians can use, so no year is shown.

events.label: God tells Noah to build an ark
events.dating: Before the Flood, when Noah's sons were grown and married (Genesis 5:32; 6:18). Early Genesis gives no dates historians can use, so no year is shown.

events.label: The great Flood begins
events.dating: In Noah's 600th year (Genesis 7:6, 7:11). Early Genesis gives no dates historians can use, so no year is shown.

events.label: Noah's ark comes to rest on Ararat
events.dating: In the seventh month of the Flood year (Genesis 8:4). Early Genesis gives no dates historians can use, so no year is shown.

events.label: God sets the rainbow as His covenant sign
events.dating: As Noah's family came out of the ark (Genesis 9). Early Genesis gives no dates historians can use, so no year is shown.

events.label: Noah curses Canaan after his drunkenness
events.dating: After the Flood, once Noah had planted a vineyard (Genesis 9:20–25). Early Genesis gives no dates historians can use, so no year is shown.

events.label: God confuses the languages at Babel
events.dating: After the Flood, when Noah's descendants had spread out (Genesis 10:32–11:9). Early Genesis gives no dates historians can use, so no year is shown.

events.label: Terah moves his family from Ur to Haran

events.label: God calls Abram to leave Haran
events.dating: About 2140–1638 BC. Abram was 75 when he left Haran (Genesis 12:4). The range is wide because it counts back from the Exodus, which is dated about 1446 or about 1260 BC, and Exodus 12:40's 430 years are read two ways.

anchor.note: Open early edge: Job gives no date. Upper edge from Ezekiel 14:14, which names Job beside Noah and Daniel; Ezekiel's dated prophecies of that period begin in 593/592 BC (Ezekiel 1:2; 8:1).

events.label: Pharaoh orders Hebrew baby boys drowned
events.dating: About 1852–1288 BC. After Joseph and his generation had died and a new king arose (Exodus 1:6–8), and before Moses was born. Scholars date the Exodus about 1446 BC (from 1 Kings 6:1) or about 1260 BC (from Egyptian history), so the range is wide.

anchor.note: Lower edge: Joseph's earliest death year (his window -1962..-1462 plus 110 = -1852; Exodus 1:6-8 puts the decree after his generation died). Upper edge: Moses' latest birth year, -1288 (Exodus 2:1-2 puts his birth under the decree).

events.label: Moses is born and hidden in a basket
events.dating: About 1575–1288 BC. Eighty years before the Exodus (Exodus 7:7). Scholars date the Exodus about 1446 BC (from 1 Kings 6:1) or about 1260 BC (from Egyptian history), so the range is wide.

events.label: Moses kills an Egyptian and flees to Midian
events.dating: About 1535–1248 BC. Moses was 40 (Acts 7:23). Scholars date the Exodus about 1446 BC (from 1 Kings 6:1) or about 1260 BC (from Egyptian history), so the range is wide.

events.dating: About 1496–1208 BC. Forty years after Moses fled, just before he went to Pharaoh at 80 (Acts 7:30; Exodus 7:7). Scholars date the Exodus about 1446 BC (from 1 Kings 6:1) or about 1260 BC (from Egyptian history), so the range is wide.

events.dating: About 563–560 BC. In the year Evil-merodach became king (2 Kings 25:27), 562/561 BC; the thirty-seventh year of Jehoiachin's exile.

events.label: Belshazzar sees the writing on the wall
events.dating: About 540–538 BC. Belshazzar was killed that night (Daniel 5:30), when Babylon fell to the Persians in 539 BC (Babylonian Chronicle).

events.label: Cyrus lets the exiles go home
events.dating: About 539–536 BC. 'The first year of Cyrus' over Babylon (Ezra 1:1), after he took the city in 539 BC (Babylonian Chronicle); Ussher dates it 536 BC.

events.label: The returned exiles rebuild the altar
events.dating: About 538–535 BC. In the seventh month after the exiles came home (Ezra 3:1).

anchor.note: The seventh month after the return under Cyrus's decree (Ezra 3:1), 538/537 BC; Ussher 536 BC.

events.label: The new temple's foundation is laid
events.dating: About 537–534 BC. In the second year after the exiles came home (Ezra 3:8).

anchor.note: The second month of the second year after the return (Ezra 3:8): 537/536 BC, Ussher 535 BC.

events.label: Daniel is thrown into the lions' den
events.dating: About 539–530 BC. Under 'Darius the Mede', soon after Babylon fell; who he was is debated (his page dates him 538–536 BC; some identify him with Cyrus, who ruled Babylon until 530 BC).

events.label: Haggai stirs the people to rebuild
events.dating: About 521–519 BC. The second year of King Darius (Haggai 1:1, 1:15), usually dated 520 BC.

events.label: The second temple is finished
events.dating: About 517–515 BC. The month of Adar in the sixth year of King Darius (Ezra 6:15), usually dated 515 BC.

events.label: Queen Vashti refuses the king's summons
events.dating: About 484–482 BC. The third year of Xerxes (Esther 1:3). Xerxes's page dates his reign from 486 or 485 BC.

events.label: Esther becomes queen
events.dating: About 480–478 BC. The tenth month of Xerxes's seventh year (Esther 2:16). Xerxes's page dates his reign from 486 or 485 BC.

events.label: Mordecai uncovers a plot to kill the king
events.dating: About 480–473 BC. After Esther became queen (Esther 2:22) and before Haman's plot in the twelfth year of Xerxes (3:7).

events.label: Haman is hanged on his own gallows
events.dating: About 475–473 BC. The twelfth year of Xerxes (Esther 3:7). Xerxes's page dates his reign from 486 or 485 BC.

events.label: The Jews celebrate the first Purim
events.dating: About 475–472 BC. The month of Adar after Haman's fall (Esther 9:1, 9:17), at the end of Xerxes's twelfth year.

events.label: Ezra arrives in Jerusalem
events.dating: About 459–397 BC. 'The seventh year of King Artaxerxes' (Ezra 7:7) is 458 BC if it means Artaxerxes I, the traditional view, or 398 BC if it means Artaxerxes II, a view many scholars hold. So its order against Nehemiah's work is disputed.

events.label: Nehemiah asks the king to send him to Judah
events.dating: About 446–443 BC. In the month of Nisan. The twentieth year of Artaxerxes (Nehemiah 2:1). His page also lists Artaxerxes II, but Nehemiah worked with the high priest Eliashib (Nehemiah 3:1) and faced Sanballat, which fixes it in Artaxerxes I's reign, 445/444 BC (an outside date). Ezra's date is disputed, so the two are never compared.

events.label: Nehemiah rebuilds Jerusalem's walls
events.dating: About 446–443 BC. Finished in fifty-two days (Nehemiah 6:15). The twentieth year of Artaxerxes (Nehemiah 2:1). His page also lists Artaxerxes II, but Nehemiah worked with the high priest Eliashib (Nehemiah 3:1) and faced Sanballat, which fixes it in Artaxerxes I's reign, 445/444 BC (an outside date). Ezra's date is disputed, so the two are never compared.

events.label: Ezra reads the Law to the people
events.dating: About 446–443 BC. Nehemiah 8 sets it in the seventh month, just after the wall was finished, with Nehemiah present. (Scholars who date Ezra's arrival to 398 BC also move this reading later.)

anchor.note: The text places it in the seventh month straight after the wall was finished (Nehemiah 6:15; 7:73-8:2), with Nehemiah present as governor (8:9): 445/444 BC under Artaxerxes I.

events.label: Nehemiah throws Tobiah out of the temple
events.dating: About 434–420 BC. After Nehemiah's return to the king in Artaxerxes's thirty-second year (Nehemiah 13:6), 'some time later'.

anchor.note: Nehemiah went back to the king in Artaxerxes I's thirty-second year, 433/432 BC (Nehemiah 13:6; 5:14), and returned 'some time later'.

events.label: An angel appears to Zechariah in the temple
events.dating: About 9–3 BC: some fifteen months before Jesus' birth (Luke 1:24–26), which came before Herod's death in 4 BC, or 1 BC on a minority view.

anchor.note: About fifteen months before Jesus' birth (Luke 1:24-26, 1:36), whose window is about 7-2 BC.

events.label: The angel Gabriel visits Mary
events.dating: About 8–3 BC: in the sixth month of Elizabeth's pregnancy (Luke 1:26), some nine months before Jesus' birth.

anchor.note: About nine months before Jesus' birth (Luke 1:26, 1:31), whose window is about 7-2 BC.

events.label: John the Baptist is born
events.dating: About 8–2 BC: about six months before Jesus' birth (Luke 1:36).

anchor.note: About six months before Jesus' birth (Luke 1:36), whose window is about 7-2 BC; inside John's people window (-10..-1).

events.label: Jesus is born in Bethlehem
events.dating: About 7–2 BC: before the death of Herod the Great (Matthew 2:1, 2:19), which most date to 4 BC and a minority to 1 BC. How the census under Quirinius (Luke 2:2) fits is debated.

events.label: Shepherds visit the baby in the manger
events.dating: About 7–2 BC: the night Jesus was born (Luke 2:11).

anchor.note: The night of Jesus' birth (Luke 2:11, 2:16); same window as the birth.

events.label: Simeon holds the baby Jesus in the temple
events.dating: About 7–2 BC: forty days after Jesus' birth, when Mary's purification was complete (Luke 2:22).

anchor.note: Forty days after the birth (Luke 2:22; Leviticus 12:2-4); same window as the birth.

events.label: Wise men bring gifts to the child Jesus
events.dating: About 7–2 BC: after Jesus' birth and before Herod's death in 4 BC (or 1 BC on a minority view).

anchor.note: After the birth and before Herod's death (4 BC, or 1 BC on a minority view).

events.label: Joseph flees to Egypt with Mary and Jesus
events.dating: About 7–2 BC: after the wise men left and before Herod's death in 4 BC (or 1 BC on a minority view).

anchor.note: After the Magi left and before Herod's death (4 BC, or 1 BC on a minority view).

events.label: Herod kills the boys of Bethlehem
events.dating: About 7–2 BC: Herod killed the boys two years old and under (Matthew 2:16), shortly before his own death in 4 BC (or 1 BC).

anchor.note: Shortly before Herod's death (4 BC, or 1 BC on a minority view).

events.label: Herod the Great dies
events.dating: About 4–1 BC: Josephus's account puts Herod's death in 4 BC on most reckonings; a minority argue for 1 BC.

events.label: The family settles in Nazareth after Egypt
events.dating: About 4 BC–AD 2: soon after Herod's death, while his son Archelaus ruled Judea (Matthew 2:22).

anchor.note: Soon after Herod's death (4 BC or 1 BC), while Archelaus ruled Judea (4 BC-AD 6), Matthew 2:22.

events.label: The boy Jesus stays behind in the temple
events.dating: About AD 5–12: when Jesus was twelve (Luke 2:42), counting from a birth in about 7–2 BC.

anchor.note: Jesus aged twelve (Luke 2:42): birth about 7-2 BC plus 12 years gives AD 6-11, widened a year each side.

events.label: John the Baptist begins preaching
events.dating: About AD 25–29: "the fifteenth year of Tiberius" (Luke 3:1) is AD 28/29 counted from his sole rule in AD 14, or about AD 26 counted from his co-regency with Augustus.

events.label: Jesus is baptised in the Jordan
events.dating: About AD 25–30: soon after John began preaching, when Jesus was "about thirty" (Luke 3:23).

anchor.note: Soon after John began preaching (Luke 3:1-3, 3:21-23; AD 25-29), when Jesus was about thirty.

events.label: Jesus is tempted in the wilderness
events.dating: About AD 25–30: straight after the baptism (Mark 1:12).

anchor.note: Straight after the baptism (Mark 1:12-13).

events.label: Jesus turns water into wine at Cana
events.dating: About AD 25–30: within a week of John's testimony about Jesus' baptism (John 1:29–2:1).

anchor.note: Within days of John's testimony after the baptism (John 1:29-2:1).

events.label: Nicodemus visits Jesus by night
events.dating: About AD 26–31: at the first Passover of Jesus' ministry in John's Gospel (John 2:13, 2:23).

anchor.note: At the first Passover of the ministry in John (John 2:13, 2:23).

events.label: Jesus meets the Samaritan woman at the well
events.dating: About AD 26–32: on the way from Judea back to Galilee after that Passover (John 4:3).

anchor.note: On the way from Judea to Galilee after that Passover (John 4:3-6).

events.label: Jesus heals an official's son from Cana
events.dating: About AD 26–32: soon after the visit to Samaria (John 4:43–54).

anchor.note: Soon after the stay in Samaria (John 4:43-54).

events.label: Herod throws John the Baptist into prison
events.dating: About AD 26–32: early in Jesus' ministry, after the time of John 3:24 and before Jesus' preaching in Galilee (Mark 1:14).

anchor.note: Early in the ministry: after the time of John 3:24, before the Galilean preaching (Mark 1:14).

events.label: Jesus calls fishermen to follow him
events.dating: About AD 26–32: early in the Galilean ministry, after John's arrest (Mark 1:14–16).

anchor.note: Early in the Galilean ministry, after John's arrest (Mark 1:14-16).

events.label: Jesus preaches the Sermon on the Mount
events.dating: About AD 26–33: during the Galilean ministry; its exact place among the other Galilean events is not fixed.

anchor.note: During the Galilean ministry; its place among other Galilean events is not fixed.

events.label: Jesus calms a storm on the lake
events.dating: About AD 26–33: during the Galilean ministry.

anchor.note: During the Galilean ministry.

events.label: John the Baptist is beheaded
events.dating: About AD 26–32: before the feeding of the five thousand (Matthew 14:13), which was near a Passover a year or more before the crucifixion.

anchor.note: Before the feeding of the five thousand (Matthew 14:12-13), which was near a Passover at least a year before the crucifixion.

events.label: Jesus feeds the five thousand
events.dating: About AD 27–32: "the Passover was near" (John 6:4), at least a year before the crucifixion in AD 30 or 33.

anchor.note: "The Passover was near" (John 6:4), at least a year before the crucifixion (AD 30 or 33).

events.label: Jesus walks on the water
events.dating: About AD 27–32: the night after the feeding of the five thousand (Matthew 14:22–25).

anchor.note: The night after the feeding (Matthew 14:22-25).

events.label: Peter declares Jesus is the Christ
events.dating: About AD 27–33: after the feeding of the five thousand, in the last year or so of the ministry.

anchor.note: After the feeding of the five thousand, in the last year or so of the ministry.

events.label: Jesus is transfigured on the mountain
events.dating: About AD 27–33: six days after Peter's confession (Matthew 17:1).

anchor.note: Six days after Peter's confession (Matthew 17:1).

events.label: Jesus raises Lazarus from the dead
events.dating: About AD 28–33: shortly before Jesus' last Passover (John 11:55).

anchor.note: Shortly before Jesus' last Passover (John 11:55, 12:1).

events.label: Zacchaeus climbs a tree to see Jesus
events.dating: About AD 28–33: on Jesus' last journey up to Jerusalem (Luke 19:1, 19:28).

anchor.note: On the last journey up to Jerusalem (Luke 19:1, 19:28).

events.label: Mary anoints Jesus' feet at Bethany
events.dating: About AD 30–33: six days before the Passover at which Jesus died (John 12:1).

anchor.note: Six days before the Passover of the crucifixion (John 12:1), AD 30 or 33.

events.label: Jesus rides into Jerusalem on a donkey
events.dating: About AD 30–33: "the next day" after the anointing at Bethany (John 12:12), in the week of the crucifixion.

anchor.note: "The next day" after the anointing (John 12:12), in the week of the crucifixion.

events.label: A poor widow gives two small coins
events.dating: About AD 30–33: in the temple courts during Jesus' last week (Mark 12:41).

anchor.note: In the temple courts in Jesus' last week (Mark 12:41).

events.label: Judas agrees to betray Jesus for silver
events.dating: About AD 30–33: two days before the Passover (Mark 14:1, 14:10).

anchor.note: Two days before the Passover (Mark 14:1, 14:10).

events.label: Jesus shares the Last Supper
events.dating: About AD 30–33: the night before the crucifixion (Mark 14:12–17).

anchor.note: The night before the crucifixion (Mark 14:12-17).

events.label: Jesus prays in Gethsemane
events.dating: About AD 30–33: the night of the Last Supper (Mark 14:26–32).

anchor.note: The night of the Last Supper (Mark 14:26-32).

events.label: Peter denies knowing Jesus
events.dating: About AD 30–33: the night of Jesus' arrest, before the rooster crowed (Mark 14:72).

anchor.note: The night of the arrest (Mark 14:66-72).

events.label: Jesus stands trial before Pilate
events.dating: About AD 30–33: early on the morning of the crucifixion (Mark 15:1).

anchor.note: Early on the morning of the crucifixion (Mark 15:1).

events.label: Jesus is crucified
events.dating: About AD 30–33: scholars mostly favour AD 30 or AD 33, years in which the Passover fell as the Gospels describe while Pontius Pilate governed Judea (AD 26–36).

events.label: Jesus is buried in Joseph's tomb
events.dating: About AD 30–33: the evening of the crucifixion (Mark 15:42).

anchor.note: The evening of the crucifixion (Mark 15:42).

events.label: The women find the tomb empty
events.dating: About AD 30–33: the first day of the week, the third day after the crucifixion (Luke 24:1).

anchor.note: The first day of the week, the third day after the crucifixion (Luke 24:1, 24:7).

events.label: Mary Magdalene meets the risen Jesus
events.dating: About AD 30–33: the morning of the resurrection (John 20:1, 20:11–16).

anchor.note: The morning of the resurrection (John 20:1, 20:11-16).

events.label: Jesus walks with two on the road to Emmaus
events.dating: About AD 30–33: "that same day", the day of the resurrection (Luke 24:13).

anchor.note: "That same day", the day of the resurrection (Luke 24:13).

events.label: Thomas sees the risen Jesus
events.dating: About AD 30–33: eight days after the resurrection (John 20:26).

anchor.note: Eight days after the resurrection (John 20:26).

events.label: Jesus restores Peter at breakfast by the lake
events.dating: About AD 30–33: after the risen Jesus' second appearance to the disciples (John 21:14), within the forty days before the ascension.

anchor.note: After the second appearance to the disciples (John 21:14), within the forty days (Acts 1:3).

events.label: Jesus is taken up into heaven
events.dating: About AD 30–33: forty days after the resurrection (Acts 1:3).

anchor.note: Forty days after the resurrection (Acts 1:3).

events.label: Matthias is chosen to replace Judas
events.dating: About AD 30–33: between the ascension and Pentecost (Acts 1:12–26).

anchor.note: Between the ascension and Pentecost (Acts 1:12-26).

events.label: The Holy Spirit comes at Pentecost
events.dating: About AD 30–33: at Pentecost, fifty days after the Passover at which Jesus died.

anchor.note: Pentecost, fifty days after the Passover of the crucifixion.

events.label: Peter heals a lame man at the temple gate
events.dating: About AD 30–35: in the first days of the Jerusalem church (Acts 3).

anchor.note: In the first days of the Jerusalem church (Acts 3).

events.label: Ananias and Sapphira fall dead
events.dating: About AD 30–36: in the early years of the Jerusalem church (Acts 5).

anchor.note: In the early years of the Jerusalem church (Acts 5).

events.label: Stephen is stoned to death
events.dating: About AD 30–37: before Saul's conversion, which most date to about AD 31–36 from Galatians 1:18 and 2:1.

anchor.note: Before Saul's conversion (Acts 8:1, 9:1), itself about AD 31-36 from Galatians 1:18 and 2:1.

events.label: Philip baptises an Ethiopian official
events.dating: About AD 30–37: soon after Stephen's death scattered the believers (Acts 8:1–5).

anchor.note: Soon after Stephen's death scattered the believers (Acts 8:1-5).

events.label: Saul meets Jesus on the Damascus road
events.dating: About AD 30–37: Galatians 1:18 and 2:1 count three and fourteen years from it to Paul's later visits to Jerusalem; most date it about AD 31–36.

anchor.note: Galatians 1:18 and 2:1 count three and fourteen years to later Jerusalem visits, the council being about AD 47-51; Aretas IV (2 Corinthians 11:32) died about AD 40.

events.label: Peter preaches to Cornelius the centurion
events.dating: About AD 31–44: after Saul's conversion and before Herod Agrippa I's death in AD 44 (Acts 9–12).

anchor.note: After Saul's conversion and before Herod Agrippa I's death in AD 44 (Acts 9-12).

events.label: Believers are first called Christians
events.dating: About AD 34–47: Saul came from Tarsus some years after his conversion (Galatians 1:18–21) and taught at Antioch for a full year (Acts 11:26).

anchor.note: Saul came from Tarsus some years after his conversion (Galatians 1:18-21) and taught a full year (Acts 11:26), before the first journey.

events.label: Herod has the apostle James killed
events.dating: About AD 41–44: Herod Agrippa I ruled Judea from AD 41 until his death in AD 44 (Josephus).

events.label: An angel frees Peter from prison
events.dating: About AD 41–44: shortly after James was killed (Acts 12:3), while Herod Agrippa I ruled Judea, AD 41–44 (Josephus).

events.label: Herod Agrippa is struck down and dies
events.dating: About AD 44 (a few scholars argue for 43): Josephus describes the same sudden death at Caesarea (Antiquities 19.343–350).

events.label: Barnabas and Saul are sent out from Antioch
events.dating: About AD 43–48: after Herod Agrippa I's death (Acts 12:23–13:3) and before the Jerusalem council.

anchor.note: After Herod Agrippa I's death (Acts 12:23-13:3) and before the Jerusalem council (about AD 47-51).

events.label: The apostles meet at the Jerusalem council
events.dating: About AD 47–51: most date the council to AD 48 or 49, before Paul's stay in Corinth under Gallio.

anchor.note: Most date it AD 48 or 49, before Paul's stay in Corinth under Gallio (AD 51-52).

events.label: Lydia believes Paul's message at Philippi
events.dating: About AD 48–52: early in Paul's second journey, before his stay in Corinth (Acts 16–18).

anchor.note: Early in the second journey, after the council and before Corinth (Acts 16-18).

events.label: The Philippian jailer is baptised
events.dating: About AD 48–52: at Philippi early in Paul's second journey, before his stay in Corinth (Acts 16–18).

anchor.note: Early in the second journey, before Corinth (Acts 16-18).

events.label: Paul speaks at the Areopagus in Athens
events.dating: About AD 49–52: just before Paul reached Corinth (Acts 18:1).

anchor.note: Just before Corinth (Acts 18:1), where Paul stayed 18 months, ending under Gallio (AD 51-52).

events.label: Paul meets Aquila and Priscilla in Corinth
events.dating: About AD 49–52: Aquila and Priscilla had recently left Rome under Claudius's order expelling the Jews (Acts 18:2), usually dated AD 49; Paul's stay in Corinth ended under Gallio, AD 51–52.

anchor.note: After Claudius's expulsion of the Jews from Rome (usually AD 49, from Orosius) and about 18 months before the Gallio hearing (AD 51-53).

events.label: Paul is brought before Gallio in Corinth
events.dating: About AD 51–53: Gallio's year as proconsul of Achaia is fixed by an inscription at Delphi to AD 51–52 (some read 52–53).

events.label: A riot breaks out in Ephesus over Artemis
events.dating: About AD 52–57: at the end of Paul's two to three years in Ephesus (Acts 19:10, 20:31).

anchor.note: At the end of Paul's two to three years in Ephesus (Acts 19:10, 20:31), after Corinth.

events.label: Eutychus falls from a window and is raised
events.dating: About AD 55–58: on Paul's last journey to Jerusalem, just after Passover (Acts 20:6–7).

anchor.note: On the last journey to Jerusalem, just after Passover (Acts 20:6-7), weeks before the arrest.

events.label: Paul is seized in the temple and arrested
events.dating: About AD 56–59: two years before Festus replaced Felix (Acts 24:27), which was about AD 59–60.

anchor.note: Two years before Festus replaced Felix (Acts 24:27); Festus arrived about AD 59-60.

events.label: Paul appeals to Caesar before Festus
events.dating: About AD 59–60: just after Festus arrived as governor (Acts 25:1), which most date to AD 59 or 60.

events.label: Paul speaks before King Agrippa
events.dating: About AD 59–60: a few days after Paul's appeal, early in Festus's governorship (Acts 25:13).

events.label: Paul is shipwrecked on Malta
events.dating: About AD 59–60: in the autumn after Festus arrived, "after the Fast" (Acts 27:9).

events.label: Paul arrives in Rome
events.dating: About AD 60–61: in the spring after the shipwreck, after three months on Malta (Acts 28:11).

events.label: John receives a vision on Patmos
events.dating: About AD 64–96: Revelation is dated either to Nero's reign (by AD 68) or, as most hold, to Domitian's (about AD 95).
